deck_name: 02 - CPTC AAT: Java OOP, C++ & Data Structures (CPW 140/141, 228, 245)

cards.prompt: In Java, which keyword prevents a class from being subclassed (inherited)?
cards.explanation: Declaring a class as 'final' (e.g., public final class MathUtils) prohibits inheritance.

cards.prompt: In Java, what keyword is used inside a subclass constructor to explicitly invoke its parent class constructor?
cards.explanation: super(...) must be the very first statement in a subclass constructor.

cards.prompt: In Java, which interface must a class implement to define a natural ordering via its compareTo(T o) method?
cards.explanation: java.lang.Comparable<T> defines int compareTo(T o) for natural sorting in Collections.sort().

cards.prompt: In Java Collections, which Set implementation maintains insertion order while preventing duplicates?
cards.explanation: HashSet makes no ordering guarantees, TreeSet sorts elements, and LinkedHashSet preserves insertion order using a doubly-linked list.

cards.prompt: In Java, what is the difference between checked and unchecked exceptions regarding compiler enforcement?
cards.answer: Checked exceptions must be caught or declared with throws
accepted_answers: Checked exceptions must be caught or declared with throws
Checked exceptions are checked at compile time
Checked exceptions require try-catch or throws
cards.explanation: Subclasses of Exception (excluding RuntimeException) are checked at compile time; RuntimeException and Error subclasses are unchecked.

cards.prompt: In C++, what is the idiom where resource acquisition (memory, file handles, mutexes) is tied to object lifetime and released in the destructor?
cards.explanation: RAII (Resource Acquisition Is Initialization) guarantees deterministic cleanup when stack objects go out of scope, even during exceptions.

cards.prompt: In Modern C++ (<memory>), which smart pointer enforces exclusive single ownership and cannot be copied (only moved)?
cards.explanation: std::unique_ptr<T> has zero overhead over a raw pointer and deletes its managed object automatically when destroyed.

cards.prompt: In C++, what keyword must precede a base class destructor when deleting derived objects through a base class pointer?
cards.explanation: Without a virtual base destructor, deleting a derived object via Base* causes undefined behavior and skips the derived destructor.

cards.prompt: In C++, what is the Rule of Three (or Rule of Five in C++11+)?
cards.answer: If a class defines a custom destructor, copy constructor, or copy assignment operator, it should define all three
accepted_answers: If a class defines a custom destructor, copy constructor, or copy assignment operator, it should define all three
Destructor, copy constructor, copy assignment operator
Custom destructor, copy constructor, and copy assignment
cards.explanation: Classes managing raw resources need custom copy/move semantics to avoid shallow-copy double-free bugs (Rule of Zero prefers smart pointers instead).

cards.prompt: In C++, which operator must be paired with memory allocated via 'new int[10]'?
cards.explanation: Array allocations made with new[] must always be freed with delete[] (never plain delete) to avoid undefined behavior.

cards.prompt: What is the worst-case time complexity (Big-O) of Binary Search on a sorted array of n elements?
cards.explanation: Each comparison halves the remaining search interval, taking at most floor(log2(n)) + 1 steps.

cards.prompt: What is the average-case vs. worst-case lookup time complexity (Big-O) of a Hash Table?
cards.explanation: With a good hash function and low load factor, lookup is O(1); if all keys collide into one bucket, it degrades to O(n).

cards.prompt: Which tree traversal order visits nodes in ascending sorted order on a valid Binary Search Tree (BST)?
cards.explanation: In-order traversal visits Left Subtree -> Root -> Right Subtree, yielding keys in non-decreasing sorted order.

cards.prompt: Which linear data structure follows LIFO (Last-In, First-Out) ordering, and what are its two primary O(1) operations?
cards.explanation: A Stack supports O(1) push (insert at top) and O(1) pop (remove from top).

cards.prompt: Which linear data structure follows FIFO (First-In, First-Out) ordering, and what are its two primary operations?
cards.explanation: A Queue inserts at the rear (enqueue) and removes from the front (dequeue).

cards.prompt: What is the time complexity of inserting at the head of a singly linked list vs. accessing the k-th element by index?
cards.answer: Head insert: O(1), Index access: O(n)
accepted_answers: Head insert: O(1), Index access: O(n)
cards.explanation: Linked lists have non-contiguous nodes, so head pointer updates take O(1) while random index traversal requires walking k nodes in O(n).

cards.prompt: Which data structure underlies a Priority Queue and provides O(log n) insertion and O(1) peek at the min/max element?
cards.explanation: A Binary Heap is a complete binary tree stored compactly in an array satisfying the heap-order property.

cards.prompt: What is the worst-case time complexity of QuickSort vs. MergeSort?
cards.answer: QuickSort: O(n^2), MergeSort: O(n log n)
accepted_answers: QuickSort: O(n^2), MergeSort: O(n log n)
QuickSort O(n^2), MergeSort O(n log n)
cards.explanation: QuickSort degrades to O(n^2) on unbalanced pivots (e.g., already sorted input with naive pivot), whereas MergeSort guarantees O(n log n) worst-case.

cards.prompt: Which graph traversal algorithm explores neighbors level-by-level using a Queue and finds shortest paths in unweighted graphs?
cards.explanation: BFS uses a FIFO queue to visit vertices in order of distance (hop count) from the source node.

cards.prompt: What happens to a Binary Search Tree's search time complexity if keys are inserted in strictly ascending sorted order without self-balancing?
accepted_answers: It becomes a linked list with O(n) lookup
cards.explanation: Without AVL or Red-Black balancing, sorted insertions produce a right-skewed degenerate tree of height n - 1.
